We must write JUnit 4 (using @Test, expected exceptions, assertEquals etc). Need to import necessary classes. Since Whitelist is in package org.jsoup.safety, tests can be in same package or import.

We'll need to test methods: static none(), simpleText(), basic(), basicWithImages(), relaxed(), constructor, addTags, removeTags, addAttributes, removeAttributes, addEnforcedAttribute, removeEnforcedAttribute, preserveRelativeLinks, addProtocols, removeProtocols, isSafeTag (protected), isSafeAttribute (protected), testValidProtocol (private), isValidAnchor (private), getEnforcedAttributes (package-private), maybe also internal behavior.

Since protected methods need subclass or reflection to test. We can create a subclass in test to expose them.

Edge cases: null arguments causing Validate.notNull etc -> expect IllegalArgumentException (Validate throws IllegalArgumentException). So test that passing null to addTags, removeTags, addAttributes (null tag), addAttributes null attributes, empty attributes array, etc throws IllegalArgumentException.

Test addAttributes with :all tag.

Test removeAttributes with :all.

Test addEnforcedAttribute and getEnforcedAttributes returns correct map.

Test removeEnforcedAttribute removal.

Test preserveRelativeLinks toggles flag (affects testValidProtocol). Could test that relative link is resolved and attribute value changed when preserveRelativeLinks false.

Need to create Element and Attribute for isSafeAttribute tests. Use jsoup Element: new Element(Tag.valueOf("a")). But Tag class is internal; we can create Element via new Element("a") maybe? Actually org.jsoup.nodes.Element has constructors: Element(Tag tag, String baseUri). But there is a static method new Element(Tag.valueOf("a")). We'll import org.jsoup.nodes.Element; Tag is org.jsoup.parser.Tag; use Tag.valueOf.

Construct attribute: new Attribute("href", "http://example.com").

Test isSafeAttribute for allowed attribute with protocol.

Test anchor validation.

Edge case: protocol list removal leads to exception when tag not present.

Test removeProtocols when protocols not set -> should throw IllegalArgumentException via Validate.isTrue.

Test addProtocols with null protocols -> NPE.

All right.

We'll create test class WhitelistTest with multiple @Test methods.

Use assertTrue/assertFalse.

Expose protected methods via subclass: class TestableWhitelist extends Whitelist { public boolean testIsSafeTag(String tag){ return super.isSafeTag(tag); } public boolean testIsSafeAttribute(String tag, Element el, Attribute attr){ return super.isSafeAttribute(tag, el, attr); } }

Similarly, we need to access private methods? testValidProtocol is private; we can indirectly test via isSafeAttribute.

Also test getEnforcedAttributes returns correct attributes.
